predictions.experiment: Temperature sensitivity of the non-self-opened plain register: accuracy of non-self-opened plain base answers at T 0.6 minus accuracy of non-self-opened plain base answers at T 1.0, on the same problems.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl; base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0). In P_math500 keep, for each problem_index, only the row with the smallest value of the sample column. In T3 keep one row per problem_index. Score every kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay' (a newline immediately followed by 'Okay'), else non-self-opened. Let S = the problem_index values present in both files whose kept rows are non-self-opened in both files. A06 = mean v3 score of the P_math500 rows in S. A10 = mean v3 score of the T3 rows in S. Report A06 - A10. Problems missing from either file are dropped.

predictions.experiment: How weak the non-self-opened plain register is when sampling is cooler: accuracy of non-self-opened plain base answers at T 0.6 minus accuracy of cued base answers at T 0.6 on the same problems.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and S3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl; base, cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). In each file keep, for each problem_index, only the row with the smallest value of the sample column. Score every kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A P_math500 row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay', else non-self-opened. Let S = the problem_index values whose kept P_math500 row is non-self-opened and which also have a kept F_math500 row. A = mean v3 score of the P_math500 rows in S. B = mean v3 score of the F_math500 rows in S. Report A - B. Problems missing from either file are dropped.

predictions.experiment: Accuracy gap between self-opened and non-self-opened plain base answers at T 0.6, within one file.
predictions.recipe: File: S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). Keep, for each problem_index, only the row with the smallest value of the sample column. Score each kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay', else non-self-opened. Report (mean v3 score of the self-opened rows) - (mean v3 score of the non-self-opened rows). If either group is empty, report nothing.

predictions.experiment: On MATH-500 at T 1.0, plain base answers that do not self-open but contain a self-check marker later ('Wait' or 'Hmm'): their accuracy minus cued base accuracy on the same problems.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. If T3 holds more than one row for a problem_index, keep the first in file order. Score each kept T3 row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A T3 row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay' (newline immediately followed by 'Okay'). Let L = the problem_index values of T3 rows that are not self-opened and whose full text field contains the case-sensitive substring 'Wait' or the case-sensitive substring 'Hmm' (or both), restricted to problem_index values present in per_problem.json. A = mean v3 score of the T3 rows in L. B = mean of t1_right over the per_problem.json entries in L. Report A - B. If L is empty, report nothing.

predictions.experiment: On MATH-500 at T 1.0, within the plain base answers that do not self-open: accuracy of those containing 'Wait' or 'Hmm' minus accuracy of those containing neither.
predictions.recipe: File: S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0). If more than one row exists for a problem_index, keep the first in file order. Score each kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. Drop rows that are self-opened (the first 60 characters of text contain the substring '\nOkay'). Among the remaining rows, group M = rows whose full text contains the case-sensitive substring 'Wait' or the case-sensitive substring 'Hmm'; group N = all other remaining rows. Report (mean v3 score of M) - (mean v3 score of N). If either group is empty, report nothing.

predictions.experiment: On the harder clean 328 at T 1.0, plain base answers that do not self-open but contain 'Wait' or 'Hmm': their accuracy minus cued base accuracy on the same problems.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-132922-7ba0/answers.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-132922-7ba0/answers.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0) and S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base, cue, T 1.0). In each file, if more than one row exists for a problem_index, keep the row with the smallest attempt value (or, with no attempt field, the first in file order). Use the score_v3 column as the score; a null or missing score_v3 counts 0, and cap_hit rows keep their score_v3. A plain (7ba0) row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay'. Let L = the problem_index values whose kept 7ba0 row is not self-opened and whose full text contains the case-sensitive substring 'Wait' or the case-sensitive substring 'Hmm', and which also have a kept e72c row. A = mean score_v3 of the 7ba0 rows in L. B = mean score_v3 of the e72c rows in L. Report A - B. If L is empty, report nothing.
